title: Piano by ear, singing and playing together, early repertoire
summary: He played only the black keys by ear, could sing and play at once, which got him into the Cats and the Fiddle, and did Fats Waller and Cab Calloway tunes as a kid.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I could only play in the black keys & it was all by ear. I never took a lesson in my life. I just could hear what was right & what was wrong. And that's the only

that kept me with Art Tatum. There was no music involved. I just could hear. A lot of people think that playing 4 strings is easy to play but its not. You've got to a lot of jumpin' about -- miss notes. Better run to cover when you run out of strings, As far as range...

Now the piano -- I first learned it. I don't know how I learned. I just kept foolin' around with it to accompany ourselves 'cause we did a lot of singing. So I came out, I'd say 75 to 90 % right compared to music, which I didn't know anything about, Just listenin' and playin'.

That's that I was one of the main voices. That's why they took me in the Cats and the Fiddle, because I was replacing a fella, the guy you hear, the high tenor... I was one of the few cats that could play and sing at the same time. If you notice a lot of guitar players if they're singing they don't play. If they're playin' they ain't singin'... To play them together, the coordination is very awkward, hard to do. But I could do that sing the words & make my chords & everything else.
We did Fats Waller tunes -- Honey suckle Rose. Everyday songs. I remember that
one distinctly. Cab Calloway tunes. Nothing We just did the everyday songs, extraordinary. Trio songs, like the Andrews Sisters.
